read.sections.0.text.source: AI stands for artificial intelligence, and artificial means made by people. AI is a big field of computer science, and people have worked on it since the 1950s, as Lesson 2 shows. It covers tasks such as understanding speech, translating sentences and recognising things in photos. There are different ways to build AI. Some AI follows rules that people wrote. Much of the AI you meet today learns patterns from data instead, and this is called machine learning. People give a program many examples, such as photos, sentences or voice recordings, and the program finds patterns in them. Then it uses those patterns to make a prediction: a careful guess about something new. Many tools combine both approaches, using rules and learning together.
read.sections.0.text.back: AI is short for artificial intelligence, that is “kecerdasan buatan”, and “buatan” means made by people. AI is a big field in computer science, and people have worked on it since the 1950s, as Lesson 2 shows. It covers tasks such as understanding speech, translating sentences and recognising things in photos. There are different ways to build AI. Some AI follows rules written by people. Instead, much of the AI you meet today learns patterns from data, and this is called machine learning. People give the program many examples, such as photos, sentences or voice recordings, and the program looks for patterns in them. Then it uses those patterns to make a prediction: a careful guess about something new. Many tools combine both ways, that is, using rules and learning together.
read.sections.0.text.note: As before, the standard text keeps the English words “artificial intelligence” once, so learners see where the letters AI come from.

read.sections.1.text.source: Hillview Learning Centre has a voice typing tool: you speak, and it types your words. Here is how a tool like this is made and used. First, its makers gave it a huge set of data, recordings of many people speaking, each with the words written down. Next, the program found patterns, such as which sounds usually go with which words. Then, when you speak, it makes a prediction about your words. It has never heard your voice before, so it cannot simply look up the answer; it guesses from the patterns. The guess is often right, but not always. If you speak quickly, if the room is noisy, or if your voice is unlike most of its examples, it may type the wrong word. So a person still reads the words and checks them.
read.sections.1.text.back: Hillview Learning Centre has a voice typing tool: you speak, and it types your words. This is how a tool like this is made and used. First, its makers gave it a very big set of data, that is, recordings of many people speaking, each one with its words written down. Next, the program looked for patterns, such as the sounds that usually come with certain words. Then, when you speak, it makes a prediction about your words. It has never heard your voice, so it cannot simply look up the answer; it guesses based on those patterns. The guess is often right, but not always. If you speak quickly, if the room is noisy, or if your voice is not like most of its examples, it may type a word that is not right. So a person still reads and checks the words.
read.sections.1.text.note: “Often” is “selalunya” and “always” is “sentiasa” (TERMS.md). “The wrong word” is “perkataan yang tidak betul”, avoiding “salah”.

read.sections.1.simpler.source: Hillview Learning Centre has a voice typing tool. You talk, and it types. Its makers gave it lots of data. This was recordings of many people talking. The words were written down too. The program found patterns. Some sounds usually go with some words. Now you talk. It has never heard your voice. So it makes a prediction about your words. Often it is right, but not always. Fast talk or a noisy room can lead to a wrong word. So can a voice that is not like its examples. So a person still checks the words.

read.sections.2.text.source: Many machines are not AI. A calculator follows fixed steps that a person wrote: it always gives 12 for 7 + 5, and it never learned that from examples. But following rules, or giving the same answer every time, does not prove a tool is not AI. Some AI uses rules, and some AI tools can be set to give the same answer each time. The word “smart” on a box does not tell you either. AI can seem clever, but it does not think or feel like a person. People decide what an AI tool is for, what data it learns from and when to trust it. So you can ask three questions about any AI tool. What does it guess? What examples did it learn from? Who checks whether it is right?
read.sections.2.text.back: Many machines are not AI. A calculator follows fixed steps written by someone: it always gives 12 for 7 + 5, and it never learned that from examples. But following rules, or giving the same answer every time, does not prove a tool is not AI. Some AI uses rules, and some AI tools can be set to give the same answer every time. The word “smart” on a box does not tell you either. AI can seem clever, but it does not think or feel like a person. People decide what an AI tool is for, what data it learns from and when it can be trusted. So you can ask three questions about any AI tool. What does it guess? What examples did it learn from? Who checks whether it is right?

write.example.source: The tool I chose is a translation tool. It guesses how to say a sentence in another language. It learned from many sentences in two languages. It found patterns in them, so it can guess a sentence it has never seen. It may be wrong with a rare word or a joke. The person who should check it is someone who speaks both languages well, before the words go into an important notice.
write.example.back: The tool I chose is a translation tool. It guesses how to say a sentence in another language. It learned from many sentences in two languages. It found patterns in them, so it can guess a sentence it has never seen. It may be mistaken with a rarely used word or with a joke. The person who should check it is someone fluent in both languages, before the words are put into an important notice.

watch.summary.source: In this short video, two people who work with AI talk about machine learning. AI is already part of everyday life. It helps choose what people see online, for example when they search. Many people imagine AI as a robot that thinks like a person. The speakers say that kind of AI is still many years away. Most AI today is machine learning. In the past, people had to write every step for a computer. With machine learning, people give the computer lots of examples. The computer finds patterns in the examples by itself. This is a bit like how you learn from practice. It is a new way to get computers to do useful jobs.

educatorNotes.0.source: There is no single agreed line between AI and other programs (see the OECD source). AI is a broad field: Stanford HAI calls it computer systems that do tasks with human-like intelligence, and says modern AI often works by finding patterns in data. This lesson teaches that common modern kind (machine learning) through one worked example; rule-based AI, such as the 1980s expert systems in Lesson 2, is AI too, and many tools mix rules and learning. If a learner asks whether a particular tool is AI, “it depends on how it was built” is often the honest answer.
